newsitem.title: TURKEY: Tanker set to leave Turkish port with Iraqi oil.
newsitem.headline: Tanker set to leave Turkish port with Iraqi oil.

text.p: The first tanker under the second term of Iraq's oil-for-food deal was set to leave the Turkish Mediterranean port of Ceyhan on Friday afternoon, a pipeline official said.
"Arcadia will leave at around 1 p.m. (1000 GMT) after the completion of filling," Fatih Sen, an official at Turkey's state pipeline company Botas, told Reuters.
He said another vessel, New Horizon, contracted by the U.S. company Coastal, would be ready to start loading at about 2 p.m. (1100 GMT) after the departure of Arcadia.

Arcadia, which began lifting oil on Wednesday evening, loaded 2.1 million barrels in the first scheduled lifting of Iraqi Kirkuk oil under the second term of the U.N.-monitored oil-for-food deal expiring on December 8.
The Maltese-flagged Arcadia, contracted by the U.S. company Bayoil, is the first ship to be loaded with Iraqi crude since late May under the United Nations sponsored oil deal.
Iraq has to sell about 1.5 million barrels per day until September 5, when the first 90 days of the second six-month deal ends.
